messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Hosted inference p99 latency spike >1200ms observed across us-west-2 streaming endpoints. Paging oncall-eng.

sara (oncall): Acked, I'm on. What's the current scope?

raj (sre): I'm seeing a correlated increase in correctable ECC errors on gpu-node-044 and thermal sensors climbing. Metric spikes started ~18:06 UTC.

mike (runtime): Streaming-side reports: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~1300ms for /v1/stream. Stalls cluster around token ~512, KV cache fetchs land on node-044 a lot.

beth (customer-ops): Customer reports incoming — a few enterprise tenants seeing timeouts on long streaming responses. Any ETA yet? :grimacing:

sara (oncall): Initial impact: hosted API streaming routes. Dedicated capacity unaffected. Rolling fallback attempted but many sessions pinned to existing worker pods.

lee (infra): Looking at node telemetry: temp rising -> fan speed up -> NVML reporting corrected ECCs. Recommend immediate cordon + drain and route traffic off node-044.

raj (sre): Agreed. Proposed mitigation: cordon node -> drain pods -> mark node quarantined -> re-route traffic to burst pool. Runbook steps below.

raj (sre): ````
# cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-node-044
# graceful drain
kubectl drain gpu-node-044 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
# mark in inventory
infra-tool node-mark --node gpu-node-044 --state quarantined --tag thermal-ecc
````

mike (runtime): Before drain finishes, flip routing policy to avoid node-044 and increase hosted burst capacity in us-west-2: `rctl route update --avoid-node gpu-node-044 --scale burst 2x`

sara (oncall): Doing cordon now.

(sara executes)

sara (oncall): cordon complete for gpu-node-044. Initiating drain.

-- logs during drain --
```
Mar 15 18:06:12 gpu-node-044 nvml: ECC corrected error count increased by 120 in 5m
Mar 15 18:07:02 kernel: GPU thermal zone 0 critical temp reached
kubectl evict pod streaming-worker-21 from gpu-node-044
pod streaming-worker-21 eviction: succeeded
```

raj (sre): ECC correction rate still rising during drain. Thermal ~85C now. We should speed up evacuation; prolonged heat + ECC is risky.

mike (runtime): Implementing hot-failover for new streaming sessions -> route to cpu-shard fallback and to other GPU pool. In-flight sessions: try to replay prefixes where possible, otherwise notify clients of stall.

beth (customer-ops): Messaging customers: "We're experiencing degraded streaming latency due to a hardware issue; we're evacuating the affected node and routing traffic to spare capacity. Estimated mitigation 15-25m." Sending now.

lee (infra): Assigning two spare GPUs from dedicated pool to hosted burst. Command: `infra-tool capacity-assign --from dedicated-pool-B --to hosted-burst 2gpus`. ETA ~5m.

(some minutes pass)

lee (infra): Capacity assign complete. Rescheduling pods from drain now.

mike (runtime): Pods rescheduled successfully. p99 fell to ~320ms within ~6 minutes post-evacuation. p95 ~140ms. Streaming stalls largely mitigated but a few tail spikes persist at token boundaries.

raj (sre): Looking at Redis/KV metrics — sudden cache misses from node-044's evicted entries. Suggest running cache scrub and consistency checks; stale or corrupted entries might cause token boundary stalls.

mike (runtime): Running scrub now: ````
runtime-tool cache-scrub --pattern /kv/node-044 --concurrency 8
````

raj (sre): Hardware ops — please open RMA. Node should be quarantined and physically inspected.

lee (infra): Ticket HW-5643 created, ops oncall notified. Node state toggled to quarantined in inventory.

beth (customer-ops): Customer update pushed: "We evacuated the impacted GPU node and routed traffic to spare capacity. Performance restored for most users; follow-up investigation and hardware replacement in progress."

mike (runtime): Postmortem action items I'm recording: 1) Add automatic preemptive drain when thermal >80C or ECC rate >X 2) Improve routing to avoid single-node hot-paths for pinned sessions 3) KV cache hardening to prevent token-boundary stalls on eviction 4) Add alert threshold for streaming stall patterns (token boundary stalling).

raj (sre): I'll own the incident writeup + perf graphs. Please attach NVML logs and scheduling traces.

sara (oncall): Incident status -> mitigated. Keeping channel open for 60m for regression watch. Closing page. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> MITIGATED at 18:42 UTC. Impact: transient p99 spikes observed by select hosted customers due to GPU node hardware (ECC/thermal) degradation. Mitigation: node evacuation and temporary capacity reallocation. Follow-up: HW-5643 (RMA), cache scrub, routing/runbook updates.
